manifest.name: dsh-plugin-background-image
manifest.description: DeepSeek Harness 界面背景图片插件（网页端与桌面端）：网络/本地图片与预设渐变背景，支持图片不透明度、沉浸式全屏/仅对话区域、毛玻璃模糊与分区不透明度调节。

bundle.text:
# 组合补丁：把本插件的行插入到 profile 的根组合中。
# dsh.plugin（profile boot）会按 dsh.profile.bundles 顺序叠加每个 bundle 的补丁。
# 该行的 id 同时是本插件设置的命名空间，客户端 plugins.row.config 的 key
# 为 <包名>#<行 id>，即 dsh-plugin-background-image#dsh-plugin-background-image。
- insert:
    - id: dsh-plugin-background-image
      name: dsh-plugin-background-image
      config: {}

readme.text:
**English** | [简体中文](https://github.com/Voyage-He/dsh-background-image/blob/main/README.zh.md)

A background image plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH), for both the Web UI and the Desktop app: set a web image, local image, or preset gradient as the interface background, with image opacity, display scope, frosted-glass blur, per-region opacity, and chat-content offset for a more immersive interface.
Adapted to **DSH 0.2.1+** (the modern Settings / Plugin Manager slots) and to **DeepSeek Harness Desktop**.

- Web images (`http(s)://`), local images (absolute paths), and `data:image/` data URLs
- **Desktop-aware local images**: in the Desktop app the native file dialog returns the real absolute path through the preload bridge; in a browser the plugin's host route opens the system dialog instead
- **Local image invalidation hint**: the referenced local file is probed automatically on page load and whenever the settings page opens; if it has been moved or deleted, a prominent hint asks you to re-pick it
- Preset gradient palettes (Aurora / Sky / Sakura / Sunset / Mint / Ocean)
- Image opacity adjustment
- Display scope: **Immersive fullscreen** / **Conversation area only**
- **Frosted-glass blur** + color saturation (applied to the sidebar and glass panels such as the composer card)
- **Conversation frosted glass**: independent blur (0–48 px) and opacity (0–100%) in both display modes; defaults to transparent with no blur to preserve existing settings
- **Readability protection**: the glass dims the image behind it in dark themes and brightens it in light themes, so sidebar labels and conversation text stay legible over very bright or very dark wallpapers
- **Per-region opacity**: sideba

<!-- Screenshots use absolute GitHub URLs: the npm package page cannot render
     relative image paths, and the demo directory is excluded from the npm
     package (files) so installs don't download ~22MB of screenshots. -->

Open the **Plugins** panel from the sidebar's panel list, then add the plugin from the local directory or from npm. The Desktop app uses the `desktop` profile, for example:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile desktop add \
  dsh-plugin-background-image@file:/path/to/background-image-plugin
```

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile <profile> add \
  dsh-plugin-background-image@file:/path/to/background-image-plugin
```

For example:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile web add \
  dsh-plugin-background-image@file:/Users/your-name/projects/background-image-plugin
```

When the Plugin Manager installs a directory as a **link** (`link:…` in the profile's `package.json`), run `pnpm install` once inside that directory so the plugin can resolve its `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` dependency; otherwise the Host reports `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` and the plugin stays inactive. Installing the published package from npm installs the dependency automatically.

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-background-image
```

Start DSH with the same profile after installation and the plugin will load. Installing a new bundle can activate through HMR; replacing an already installed package requires a restart.

1. Open DSH.
2. Go to **Settings → Background Image** (a top-level tab in the settings sidebar). Alternatively, open the **Plugins** panel from the sidebar's panel list, open the **Background Image** bundle card under **Installed**, and click **Configure** on the plugin's row.
3. Enable the background, then choose a web image, a local image, or a preset gradient. For local images, clicking "Choose Local Image" opens the native system file dialog; the selected absolute path is recorded (the file stays where it is — never copied or moved).
4. Adjust the image opacity, display scope, **frosted glass** (blur strength and glass color saturation, applied to the sidebar and composer card), **per-region opacity** (sidebar, conversation area, composer), and **chat content offset** as needed. Lower opacity values are more transparent and more immersive; the sidebar shows frosted glass in immersive fullscreen, while the composer takes effect in both modes.

Both entry points use the same plugin `Config` form, so changes made in one are reflected in the other. The top-level settings page is registered through `settings.section`; the row entry uses the modern `plugins.row.config` slot (the successor of the old `settings.plugin.item` settings card).

The settings live in the plugin's `Config` and are written by the DSH settings service into the **profile patch** (`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`) as an override of the row the bundle inserts:

```yaml
- id: dsh-plugin-background-image
  config:
    enabled: true
    mode: fullscreen

Omitted fields use the schema defaults. `settings.yaml` is not used by this version; values saved by 1.2.x under the old `background-image` namespace are not read — set them once in the new config page after upgrading.

- Everything is restored automatically after a page refresh or a DSH restart.
- Local images are **recorded as absolute paths — never copied or moved**; the file stays where it is.

> Browsers cannot load `file://` resources directly due to security policies, so the plugin registers a read-only file-serving route on the host (`GET /plugins/background-image/file?path=<absolute-path>`) that serves the local image referenced by the configuration to the page over same-origin http. The route only accepts loopback origins and only serves the exact path currently referenced by the `image` field ("reference-as-authorization", the same model as the official `session.attachment`). If the image file is moved or deleted, the background stops working and the path must be set again.

- `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`: host-side `Config` schema definition and validation.
- `react` (peer, optional): client-side settings UI.
- Node.js built-ins: `node:child_process`, `node:fs/promises`, `node:path`.

- **Desktop app**: no external command is needed — the renderer's hidden file input is converted to a real path by the preload bridge (`window.__DSH_HOST_PATHS__.pathFor`).
- **Web UI**: the host opens the system dialog with the following commands:

| Platform | Required command |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | `osascript` (bundled with the system) |
| Linux | `zenity` or `kdialog` (either one is enough) |
| Windows | `powershell` |
When none of these is available, you can still type the local absolute path manually.
This plugin works by **overriding DSH theme tokens** and **injecting CSS**, which changes the global interface appearance. Keep the following in mind:

1. **Immersive fullscreen paints one fixed image layer**: the plugin sets `--dsw-alias-bg-base` and `--dsw-specific-sidebar-fill` to `transparent` and draws the image once in `body::before` (`position: fixed`). This is what makes the same image appear continuously behind the sidebar, center column, detail column, and bottom row on both the Web UI and the Desktop window — including macOS Desktop, where the window itself is transparent and uses native vibrancy. Elements that paint `--dsw-alias-bg-base` directly (for example some tool panel surfaces) become see-through to the image; elements that use `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-*` / `--dsw-alias-bg-overlay` (menus, the Settings panel, floating dialogs) stay opaque.
2. **Conversation area only** paints the image on the center column and keeps the native background elsewhere.
3. **Internal structure selectors use semantic suffixes and stable data attributes**: the plugin targets `[class*="_sidebarCol"]`, `[class*="_centerCol"]`, `[class*="_frame"]`, `[data-rightbar-col]`, `[data-shell-bottom]`, `[data-phase][class*="_root"]`, `[data-composer-seat]`, `[class*="_viewArea"]`, `[class*="_composerStack"]`, and `[class*="_composerHero"]` rather tha

Update to the latest version:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-plugin-background-image@latest
```

Uninstall the plugin:

```bash
npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove dsh-plugin-background-image
```

- Node.js 20 or later
- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1 or later** (Web UI or Desktop). Version 1.2.x targeted the older `settings.plugin.item` / `settings.register` APIs and is not compatible with 0.2.1+.
